recipes.name: Easy Chicken Fajita Soup
ingredients_raw: 1 pound skinless, boneless chicken breasts, cut into strips
1 red bell pepper, cut into thin strips
1 green bell pepper, cut into thin strips
1 poblano pepper, cut into thin strips
1 large onion, cut into thin strips
1 (14.5 ounce) can fire roasted diced tomatoes

steps.text: Heat oil in a large soup pot over medium heat. Add chicken and cook, stirring only occasionally, until brown, about 10 minutes. Sprinkle fajita seasoning over chicken and stir until well coated. Add bell peppers, poblano pepper, and onion; cook and stir over medium heat until vegetables are soft, about 10 minutes.
Pour in black beans, fire-roasted tomatoes, and chicken broth. Increase the heat to high and bring to a boil, then reduce the heat to medium-low and simmer for 30 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Season soup with hot sauce, salt, and pepper before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Easy Chicken Fajita Soup
raw_recipe.description: This chicken fajita soup cooks up quickly but delivers slow-cooked flavor, thanks to fire-roasted tomatoes, fajita seasoning, and seasoned black beans.

review.reviewBody: This soup is delicious. Just enough heat to keep it tasty. Like one of the other reviewers, I used a small can or green chiles and increased the broth to 26 oz. I also added a bag of frozen southwestern style corn I had on hand in the freezer. Before serving, I added shredded cheese on top, either mexican or mozzarella. Fantastic

Pretty awesome! I prepared this ala vegan for the ladies of the house replacing regular chicken broth with Orrington Farms Vegan Broth Base (Amazon) but did a little chicken on the side for myself. I wanted the ratio of beans to veggies to be a bit beanier so I didn't add the green bell pepper. To speed things up, I started warming the broth, beans & tomatoes in a pot while sauteeing the veggies in a pan. I added a bit of broth to the pan as when I tossed in the fajita mix onto the oil, it caked up right away. Otherwise, I stuck to the recipe. The ladies & I all loved it!

This soup is so delicious and flavorful. I actually make this in the crock pot. I cook the chicken with the oil and some garlic on the stovetop and add it in with all of the other ingredients in the crock pot. Like some of the others have recommended, I use the diced tomatoes with chile peppers and actually add an additional small can of chile peppers. And I do use more than one packet of fajita seasoning too.

I cook on high in the crock pot for 4 hours. 

I add some shredded mexican cheese, sour cream and tortilla strips on top.

Since my husband isn't a huge soup eater, he actually uses a slotted spoon to drain the liquid and uses a flour tortilla to make fajitas. 

Tastes awesome either way!

This is possibly the best soup I've ever had. The only changes I made were:
-I put pinto beans instead of black beans, because I'm not too big a fan of black beans and I happened to have a can of pinto.
-I baked and shredded a few chicken legs instead of using breasts because I didn't have any. I used three legs, but I would suggest using more than that because it wasn't very meaty.
-I put half a can of corn in after it was done cooking, just to get the corn hot, not to cook it.
-And at the end, I garnished it with some Monterey Jack cheese and some sour cream!!
It turned out amazing. I would suggest making a double batch so you have a bunch, because now I wish I had more.

This will be a new go to recipe for me! Everyone in the family loved it! Based on other reviews I made a few modifications: I used a can of green chilies instead of the pabalano pepper, added 2 cloves of minced garlic, shredded the chicken, 2 cans of black beans, 2 cans of fire roasted tomatoes, 2 packets of seasoning, doubled the broth and added a little over a cup of corn. I also topped with with fresh chopped cilantro and jalapeño, tortilla chips, and shredded Mexican cheese.

I made this and used a rotisserie chicken, a mix of green, yellow, red and orange bell peppers along with the poblano, and regular diced tomatoes, rather than fire roasted. Since my chicken was already cooked, I started by sautéing the peppers and onion. Then I added the fajita seasoning, the tomatoes and chicken broth and simmered for about 15 minutes. Then added the black beans and chicken. I didn’t simmer any further because I didn’t want my beans to get mushy. I made this early in the afternoon and refrigerated it, then reheated just before serving. I did find there was very little broth (even though I covered this while simmering), so I added another can of chicken broth before reheating. This was good fajita soup and I loved all the peppers in it. I might try this with taco seasoning next time. UPDATE 1/25/14: Made this again as follows - I did use taco seasoning this time, along with red, yellow and green pepper. This time I did not have a poblano. Instead of the fire roasted tomatoes, I used two 10 oz. cans of Rotel, which added nice heat, and I used regular black beans, rinsed and drained, not the seasoned black beans. As before I added extra chicken broth, this time using nearly an entire 32 oz. container.

This soup is absolutely delicious! I used left over rotisserie chicken from the supermarket which I added in the end instead of the beginning , I also added fresh spinach which gave it a beautiful color and juice from a whole lemon at the end which my husband loved. The hot sauce I left out as it is so tasteful already . Loved it, loved it!

Excellent recipe! I added rice to it too make it more filling. Make the rice separately and store separately. Add the rice after you're done cooking the soup to each serving. Warning: if you mix the rice with the soup and let it sit overnight, the rice will soak up the soup juice. (learned this the hard way.. lolol) I'm definitely saving this.

I will definitely make this again and soon! I used chopped green chilies (1/2 cup) instead of a poblano, added juice of one lime to each bowl along with a dollop of sour cream. Fantastic!I was afraid it would taste too much like a pepper soup but not at all, in fact, the flavors blended beautifully. I will double the recipe next time.

We really enjoyed this recipe. Made some changes based on what I had on hand, and took some others advice, used two cans of black beans, a dash of garlic, and a can of corn. We also just had regular diced tomatoes, not fire roasted, and used a can of diced jalapenos since i didn't have poblano. I went ahead and used a bag of frozen red, green and yellow peppers and onion too. I think the extra beans made it richer and thicker, and the corn gave it some nice variety (soup didn't feel as dimensional as a soup should without it). We topped with lowfat mexican four cheese blend, a dollop of light sour cream, and crushed up tortilla chips. We'll definitely be having this again!

This was one of the best soups I have ever made. I went through and read the reviews, as I always do before I make a new dish, and although the dish is probably wonderful the way it is written, if there is something that keeps coming up repeaedly, I make that change....I read to add an extra 1/2 pack of fajita seasoning and a can of dieced fire roasted green chilis...It was AMAZING!! We didnt even add any hot sauce since we have a 2 y/o who was having dinner also. We used Tostitos Artisan recipe "Toasted Southwestern Spices" chips and monterey jack cheese, and had it more like a tortilla soup and every one ate so much, their tummys were buldging out! I also doubeled the amount of soup stated so there was more broth, as my family loves the broth! Thank you for a GREAT recipe!

Added garbanzo beans, sweet corn, extra can of diced tomatoes and a cup of rice. I used 1 1/2 packets of taco seasoning as I didn’t have fajita seasoning. It was a thicker consistency which my hubby loved!
I doubled the recipe and added a dash of cayenne. In keeping with my typical mixed fajita dinner preference at mexican restaurants I used both beef and chicken. Delicious!!
So good and healthy. I added more chicken broth

I don’t know how this got 5 stars, I thought it was very bland and not much different from any other taco/Mexican soup I’ve made in the past. Quite disappointed in this recipe, clearly won’t make this again
Very flavorful and filling. I served with tortilla chips I baked with seasonings (low carb tortillas). Was a big hit and hubby requested I add to the "repeat" list.
We've made this a few times, and love it.
Everybody loved it!
Loved this soup. It is a meal by itself and healthy to boot.

2-28-19 used 1 chicken breast used both sides. cooked in 1.5 bags fajita mix. added to pot with 1 red 1 green 1 poblano pepper cut in strips. used 6 slices onion cut up fine. used 32 oz chicken broth 28 oz tomato 1 can black bean 15 oz. added 1 small can green chilies also a few mushrooms
